# Book of Giants Fragment 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4Q531 frag. 2 (Cave 4) | **Condition:** fragmentary; lamentation preserved in part

---

**10:1** [...] Woe to-us [...] for-our-sin [...]

**10:2** [...] the-judgment is-sealed [...] and-written-in-heaven [...]

**10:3** [...] and-there-is-none who-can-erase-it [...]

**10:4** [...] for-the-decree-of the-Most-High stands [...]

**10:5** [...] and-it-cannot-be-turned-back [...]

**10:6** [...] and-there-is-no escape for-us [...] neither in-heaven above [...]

**10:7** [...] nor in-the-earth below [...]

**10:8** [...] for-all the-ways are-closed before-us [...]

**10:9** [...] and-the-gates-of mercy are-shut [...]

**10:10** [...] against-our-faces [...]

**10:11** [...] our-mighty-deeds are-ended [...] and-our-power has-been-brought-low [...]

**10:12** [...] and-our-glory has-departed from-us [...]

**10:13** [...] the-strength-of our-arms is-broken [...]

**10:14** [...] and-we-cannot stand before-the-judgment [...]

**10:15** [...] for-our-sins are-too-great [...]

---

*EMET notes: Fragment 10 (Lament of the Giants). Source: 4Q531 frag. 2. Aramaic text from Cave 4 Qumran. Hyphenated compounds preserve Aramaic construct-chain syntax and bound morphemes. Square brackets indicate genuine manuscript lacunae where the leather has deteriorated or broken away. The Book of Giants is an Aramaic expansion of the Watcher myth from 1 Enoch 6-16, featuring the Nephilim giants Ohya, Hahya (sons of Shemihazah), Mahaway (son of Baraq'el), and the hero Gilgamesh.*
